uncited: Volume Ray Marching Optimization refers to a set of shader-level and rendering pipeline techniques designed to reduce the computational cost of evaluating participating media, specifically in the context of volumetric clouds.
It addresses the bottleneck of expensive material evaluations and multiple light scattering approximations during ray traversal.
Unlike general traversal optimizations that skip empty space, this method optimizes the *cost* of the density and lighting calculations performed at each sample point.

It distinguishes itself by focusing on material simplification (grayscale inputs), scattering approximation limits, and alternative shadowing strategies (cascaded shadow maps vs. secondary ray marching) rather than spatial acceleration structures.
The method operates within the fragment shader of a volumetric cloud material, typically in a real-time engine context.
It modifies the evaluation loop of the ray marcher to reduce arithmetic intensity and memory bandwidth.
- **Input:** Ray origin, ray direction, step size, material parameters (density, color, scattering coefficients), camera position, light positions.
- **Material Parameters:** Typically a vector or struct containing density, color, and scattering coefficients.
- **Conservative Density:** A scalar or vector component used for early-out culling.
Before evaluating the full material model, check the conservative density value.
This acts as a fast-path filter for low-density regions.
If the "Gray Scale Material" optimization is enabled, restrict the material's input parameter evaluation to only the Red (R) channel.
This reduces the number of texture lookups or procedural noise evaluations required per sample.
Limit the number of octaves used for the Multi-Scattering Approximation.
The default is single scattering (0 octaves).
The shader should cap this value to balance quality and performance.
- **If Enabled:** Perform secondary ray marching through the cloud volume to compute shadows.
- **If Disabled:** Use Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM).
If frame budget allows, enable Ground Contribution.
This is an additive cost for visual fidelity.
- **Conservative Density Threshold:** Default 0.0.
- **Enable Ground Contribution:** Boolean.
- **Time Complexity:** The optimization reduces the constant factor of the per-sample cost.
Conservative density culling provides an O(1) early-out.
Grayscale material evaluation reduces texture fetches.
Limiting scattering octaves reduces the complexity of the scattering function from O(N) to O(min(N, 2)).
CSM shadows replace O(M) ray marches (where M is the number of shadow samples) with a single texture lookup, significantly reducing time complexity for shadowing.
- **Memory Complexity:** No additional memory structures are introduced by the shader optimizations themselves.
Exact FPS gains are not given in the sources.
Conservative density culling may cause artifacts if not tuned.
- **When to Use:** When frame budget is tight and visual fidelity of shadows/scattering can be compromised.
When clouds are dense and material evaluation is the bottleneck.
- **When Not to Use:** When high-fidelity color shadows are required.
When ground lighting is critical for realism.
This method originates from the implementation of the Volumetric Cloud Component in Unreal Engine 5.8, as documented by Epic Games.
It is part of the engine's toolkit for optimizing real-time volumetric rendering.
The techniques are specific to the cloud material system and are not general-purpose volume rendering algorithms.
